security_audit.summary: All 276 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. Most are documentation or identifier matches; the bundled scripts perform only the documented local Instruments workflow with argument-array subprocess calls. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or command-injection intent was found.

remediation.issue: Trace recording executes local Xcode Instruments commands when explicitly requested.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command arguments as arrays, require an explicit user target, and display the proposed recording command before execution.

remediation.issue: A predictable temporary stop-file can be created by another local user to stop a recording.
remediation.suggestion: Use a per-session stop-file in a private directory when concurrent local users are a concern.

content.user_title: Improve SwiftUI Apps with Expert Guidance
content.value_statement: SwiftUI projects can develop state, identity, performance, and API compatibility problems that are difficult to diagnose. This skill provides targeted review guidance, modern platform patterns, and optional Instruments trace analysis.
actual_capabilities: Review SwiftUI state ownership, bindings, observable models, and environment usage.
Identify list and ForEach identity problems that can cause incorrect updates.
Recommend view composition and performance improvements for expensive update paths.
Check availability gating and suggest modern replacements for deprecated APIs.
Apply accessibility guidance for controls, labels, Dynamic Type, and charts.
Analyze supplied Instruments trace data for hangs, hitches, CPU hotspots, and repeated view updates.
limitations: It does not compile, run, or test an app unless the user requests and enables those actions.
Trace recording requires Xcode Instruments and an appropriate local target.
Recommendations depend on the source code and trace information that the user provides.
iOS 26 features require availability checks and fallbacks for earlier systems.

use_cases.title: Review a feature before release
use_cases.description: Find state, identity, accessibility, and API availability issues in a SwiftUI change.

use_cases.title: Improve a slow screen
use_cases.description: Use a supplied Instruments trace to prioritize view updates, hitches, and CPU work.

use_cases.title: Modernize a macOS interface
use_cases.description: Plan safe SwiftUI API migrations with platform-specific fallbacks and window guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review a SwiftUI view
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for state ownership, accessibility, and common correctness issues. Explain each recommendation simply.

prompt_templates.title: Fix list updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this List and ForEach code. Find unstable identity or update problems, then propose a safer structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an API migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify deprecated SwiftUI APIs in this code. Propose modern replacements with availability checks and fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a performance trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Instruments trace for the most important SwiftUI performance problems. Prioritize fixes using trace evidence and suggest source areas to inspect.

output_examples.input: Review a list that refreshes after editing an item.
output: Finding: The row identity changes when the title changes.
Recommendation: Store a stable identifier outside the view body.
Priority: High, because unstable identity can recreate rows.

output_examples.input: Analyze a trace with animation hitches during scrolling.
output: Priority 1: Inspect the view with the highest repeated update cost.
Evidence: The trace shows repeated work during the scrolling interval.
Next step: Move derived work outside the view body and measure again.

best_practices: Provide the relevant SwiftUI source file and the deployment target.
Ask for a prioritized explanation when reviewing a large feature.
Share a focused trace interval when investigating a specific interaction.
anti_patterns: Do not apply iOS 26 APIs without availability checks and fallbacks.
Do not use transient or mutable values as List and ForEach identity.
Do not treat trace recommendations as proof without validating the affected flow.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SwiftUI development for iOS and macOS.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant views and models for a focused review.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review hot paths and analyze a supplied Instruments trace.

faq.question: Does it require an Instruments trace?
faq.answer: No. Trace analysis is optional and source review works without one.

faq.question: Can it use iOS 26 APIs?
faq.answer: Yes, when requested and protected with availability checks and fallbacks.

faq.question: Will it modify my code automatically?
faq.answer: It should only edit code when you explicitly request edits.
